claims.text: An optimal Ru content in Pt–Ru nanoalloys produces distinct Pt–Ru surface ensembles.
Ru sites adjacent to Pt promote localized OH adsorption.
Localized OH assists the oxidative removal of poisoning intermediates such as adsorbed CO.
Removal of poisoning intermediates enables complete 12-electron oxidation of ethanol on Pt–Ru.
Balancing adsorbate binding and removal through the proposed bifunctional mechanism enhances catalytic activity and durability.
Carbon-supported Pt–Ru catalysts with non-optimized Ru content undergo partial ethanol oxidation and accumulate poisoning species.
Controlled chemical dealloying can introduce precise amounts of Ru into the Pt–Ru nanoalloy.
Atomic-resolution characterization will be used to verify the surface composition and spatial distribution of Ru.
Optimized Ru content will lower the ethanol-oxidation onset potential relative to non-optimized or spatially uncontrolled Ru.
Optimized Ru content will increase ethanol-oxidation current density.
Optimized Ru content will increase selectivity toward CO2 formation.
Optimized Ru content will improve catalyst durability.
Insufficient localized OH adsorption causes higher onset potentials, lower oxidation activity, and greater intermediate poisoning in the baseline catalysts.
The proposed mechanism is significant in carbon-supported Pt–Ru nanoalloys under fuel-cell-relevant conditions.
Loss of the Ru distribution under harsh operating conditions would suppress the proposed mechanistic effect.
The proposed mechanism may fail when poisoning pathways other than the OH-assisted removal pathway dominate.

contradictions.description: The proposal says that chemical dealloying will introduce controlled amounts of Ru, although dealloying ordinarily tunes composition by selectively removing a component. It does not explain what precursor component is removed or how the operation introduces Ru.

The hypothesis predicts an optimal Ru content, which permits non-monotonic performance, but the falsification rule demands systematic improvement as Ru content increases. Performance declining beyond an optimum would satisfy the stated hypothesis yet could trigger its falsification rule.
